name: Ollama
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Ollama runs open large language models such as Llama, Gemma and Qwen on the CPU, behind an HTTP API. Downloads the chosen models at start; its API has no login, so share the address only with apps you trust.
startup: o=./ollama/bin/ollama; [ -x $o ] || { echo "Ollama isn't installed: reinstall the server."; exit 1; }; export HOME=/home/container OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:{{SERVER_PORT}} OLLAMA_MODELS=/home/container/models; if [ "{{OLLAMA_CLOUD}}" = 1 ]; then unset OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD; else export OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1; fi; for v in OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH OLLAMA_ORIGINS; do [ -n "${!v}" ] || unset $v; done; (trap - INT TERM; exec $o serve) & pid=$!; trap : INT TERM; until curl -fs -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:{{SERVER_PORT}}/api/version; do kill -0 $pid 2>/dev/null || { wait $pid; exit; }; sleep 1; done; for m in {{MODELS}}; do $o show "$m" >/dev/null 2>&1 && continue; echo "Downloading the model $m."; $o pull "$m" </dev/null || echo "The model $m couldn't be downloaded."; done; echo "Ollama is ready on port {{SERVER_PORT}}. Type an ollama command here: list, ps, pull <model>, rm <model>, run <model> <prompt>."; while kill -0 $pid 2>/dev/null; do if read -r -t 1 -a a; then [ ${#a[@]} = 0 ] || $o "${a[@]}" </dev/null; elif [ $? -le 128 ]; then break; fi; done; wait $pid

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Ollama: downloads the release for this CPU from GitHub, checked against its
# SHA-256, and keeps only what runs on the CPU (the GPU libraries are most of
# the download, and a server here has no GPU). Downloaded models (models/)
# are never touched.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }

case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=amd64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "Ollama has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

version="${VERSION:-latest}"
[ "$version" = latest ] || version="v${version#v}"
# gh-release says why when the release doesn't exist or GitHub can't be reached.
tag=$(gh-release tag ollama/ollama "$version") || exit 1
asset="ollama-linux-${arch}.tar.zst"
mkdir -p models

if [ -x ollama/bin/ollama ] && [ "$(cat ollama/.raptor-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag" ]; then
    echo "Ollama $tag is already installed."
    exit 0
fi
sum=$(gh-release assets ollama/ollama "$tag" | awk -v a="$asset" '$1 == a { print $2 }')
[ -n "$sum" ] || fail "Ollama $tag has no build for this CPU ($asset)."

work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work/new"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
echo "Downloading Ollama $tag. Only its CPU parts (about 70 MB of the 1.5 GB) are kept."
# The archive is unpacked as it arrives, so it never takes up the disk; it's
# checked against the release's SHA-256 before anything is replaced.
mkfifo "$work/pipe"
tar --zstd -x -C "$work/new" --exclude='lib/ollama/cuda_*' --exclude='lib/ollama/rocm*' --exclude='lib/ollama/vulkan*' < "$work/pipe" &
untar=$!
curl -fsSL --retry 3 -A "raptor-installer (+https://raptorpanel.net)" \
    "https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases/download/$tag/$asset" | tee "$work/pipe" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1 > "$work/sum" ||
    fail "The download of Ollama $tag failed. Reinstall to try again."
wait "$untar" || fail "Ollama $tag's archive couldn't be unpacked. Reinstall to try again."
if [ "$sum" = - ]; then
    echo "GitHub shows no SHA-256 for $asset, so it wasn't checked."
elif [ "$(cat "$work/sum")" != "$sum" ]; then
    fail "Ollama $tag's download doesn't match its SHA-256. Reinstall to try again."
fi
[ -x "$work/new/bin/ollama" ] || fail "Ollama $tag's archive has no bin/ollama."

echo "$tag" > "$work/new/.raptor-version"
rm -rf ollama.old
[ ! -e ollama ] || mv ollama ollama.old
mv "$work/new" ollama
rm -rf ollama.old
echo "Installed Ollama $tag."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Ollama version to install, such as 0.40.16, or latest. Reinstall the server to change it.

variables.name: Models
variables.description: Models from ollama.com/library to download when the server starts, separated by spaces, such as llama3.2:1b qwen3:4b. Models you already have aren't downloaded again.

variables.name: Keep loaded
variables.description: How long a model stays in memory after its last request, such as 5m or 1h; -1 keeps it loaded.

variables.name: Parallel requests
variables.description: How many requests each model answers at once. More needs more memory.

variables.name: Context length
variables.description: The context window in tokens, unless a request sets its own. Empty lets Ollama choose from the memory it has.

variables.name: Allowed origins
variables.description: Extra web origins allowed to call the API from a browser, separated by commas, such as your chat app's address.

variables.name: Cloud features
variables.description: Allow Ollama's cloud models and web search, which send prompts to ollama.com.
